name: Blue Ribbon Lawns Inc.
niche: landscaping / lawn care (residential mowing, landscape design, mulching, tree service)

address.source: Confirmed consistently across BBB (bbb.org/us/fl/kathleen/profile/lawn-care/blue-ribbon-lawns-inc-0733-235968018), Birdeye (reviews.birdeye.com/blue-ribbon-lawns-inc-170484945526326), Houzz professional profile and the task brief. No conflicting addresses found in any directory.

phone_source: Confirmed across BBB, Birdeye, Houzz, Manta, Buzzfile, Yellow Pages and the business's own Facebook page. Identical number also appears on the Yellow Pages / website listing of a separate registered entity, Blue Ribbon Tree's LLC (blueribbontreesllc.com), also based in Kathleen FL 33849, strongly suggesting a shared family operation (tree work commonly split into its own LLC for insurance/liability reasons). This was NOT used to justify pulling Blue Ribbon Tree's branded content onto this site; it is documented here only as research context. All site copy and photos are sourced directly from Blue Ribbon Lawns Inc.'s own Facebook page.
email_search_notes: Deep search performed, no public email found. Checked: BBB profile (only generic 'Sales / Technical Support / Customer Service' message categories for BBB's own contact-business form, not real addresses), Birdeye profile (no email field), Facebook page and About subpage (fetched via facebookexternalhit and Facebot/WhatsApp/Slackbot/Telegram crawler user agents to bypass the login wall; only og:meta tags returned, no email), Houzz professional profile (no email), Manta and Dun & Bradstreet listings (both blocked with 403 on every fetch attempt, no email recoverable), Buzzfile listing (no email), Yellow Pages listing (no email). No Instagram account found to check a bio/email. No working owned domain to check (blueribbonlawns.com returns HTTP 503, see has_own_site notes). Recorded as null per pipeline rule: do not invent an email.
instagram_search_notes: Searched multiple variants ('Blue Ribbon Lawns Kathleen instagram', 'Blue Ribbon Lawns Lakeland instagram.com'). No Instagram account could be verified as belonging to this business. Unrelated accounts surfaced ('Blue Ribbon Lawn & Landscape', 'Blue Ribbon Outdoor') are different businesses in different markets, not used. Facebook is the only verified social channel.
facebook_note: Official public page, title 'Blue Ribbon Lawns Inc. | Lakeland FL', 1,144 likes, 735 check-ins ('were here'). Page is login-walled for normal browsers (curl/WebFetch with multiple crawler user agents only returned og:meta tags: title, description, single profile picture). BREAKTHROUGH: the repo's Playwright + fixed-Chrome-launch technique (per FORGE-BRIEF's ig_scrape_fixed.js pattern, adapted for facebook.com/BlueRibbonLawns/photos with --disable-quic/--ssl-version-max=tls1.2 to work through this environment's proxy) successfully rendered the public photos grid without login: 65 unique real photos recovered from tags (scontent-*.fbcdn.net URLs), each downloaded with curl and verified with `file`. Visually curated via a contact sheet: excluded all marketing graphics with text/quote overlays ('We Are Hiring', holiday greetings, 'I came I mowed I kicked grass' meme, award nomination graphics, business-card flyers), kept only real, unbranded or business-branded photographs of finished lawns, landscaping, and crew at work. 10 photos used across hero/about/gallery/logo, well above the 5-photo minimum.
own_site_check: blueribbonlawns.com: DNS resolves and TLS handshake completes at the CONNECT/proxy layer, but the origin server returns HTTP 503 Service Unavailable on both http:// and https:// (confirmed independently via curl -v through the sandbox proxy AND via the WebFetch tool, both returned 503). This is a broken/down domain, not an unregistered one: the wayback machine shows blueribbonlawns.com was live as recently as 2019-2021 (GoDaddy Website Builder template with generic stock photography, no real business photos), then returns 404 by late 2021, consistent with the hosting lapsing. blueribbonlawnsinc.com: does not resolve at all (proxy CONNECT tunnel fails with 502 Bad Gateway, i.e. no DNS/no listener). BBB's own profile explicitly does not list a website field for this business. Houzz lists 'blueribbonlawnsinc.com' as a claimed-but-unreachable website candidate. Given the domain is completely inaccessible to any visitor today (hard 503, not a redirect or partial page), has_own_site is recorded as false for outreach/registry purposes, but the outreach angle explicitly says 'your website is not loading' rather than falsely claiming they have no web presence at all, per FORGE-BRIEF's guidance on broken-domain cases.
rating_source: Birdeye (reviews.birdeye.com/blue-ribbon-lawns-inc-170484945526326), which aggregates and explicitly cites Google as its review source for this listing (Google icon shown next to each review). 5.0 average, 29 reviews. Matches the rating given in the task brief exactly.

reviews_used.author: Jacqui Bailey
reviews_used.text: I was sooo impressed with the quality of their work, the fairness of the price and the friendliness of the employees.

reviews_used.author: Peggy Osteen
reviews_used.text: Arrived on time and did an awesome job. Really knows what they are doing and do it well. Pricing was great compared to what I've paid and quoted in the past.
reviews_used.note: Verified real but not used in the final 3-quote testimonial section; Jacqui Bailey, Chris Davison and Josh Zarbaugh were selected for variety (price/quality, a specific tree-root problem solved, and a short trust-building one-liner).

reviews_used.author: Josh Zarbaugh
reviews_used.text: Great family owned business, highly recommend!

reviews_used.author: Chris Davison
reviews_used.text: This company was a great blessing to us. We had them remove our tree because the roots were getting into our drainfield system.

awards: Voted #1 Best of Central Florida 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2023, and #1 Best of the Best 2018; Top #3 Community's Choice Award 2022 and 2024. These are Central Florida Community's Choice Awards (yourchoiceawards.com/centralflorida/), a real reader-vote awards program; text repeated verbatim across the business's own Facebook About text, Houzz, Manta and BBB listings.
hours_source: Birdeye listing (Mon-Fri 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Sat-Sun closed).
years_in_business: Started 3/25/2013 per BBB (13 years in business as of 2026). Entity 'Blue Ribbon Lawns Inc.' formally incorporated in Florida 12/7/2015 per Sunbiz/OpenCorporates records (common pattern: sole proprietorship operating since 2013, later incorporated).
ownership: Rodney Joe Brown listed as registered agent/business management contact (BBB, Sunbiz). Keri Brown listed as Principal in SBA PPP loan records (federalpay.org). Likely a married couple; consistent with the Josh Zarbaugh review 'Great family owned business'. Owner names are NOT used as personal bios on the site itself since the business does not publicly present an owner bio/photo; 'family owned' is used instead, directly supported by the review.

images.method: Standard curl/WebFetch research hit a hard wall: Facebook serves only a single profile-picture og:image to anonymous requests (tested with 6+ user agents: default Chrome, facebookexternalhit, Facebot, WhatsApp, Slackbot-LinkExpanding, TelegramBot; all subpages /photos, /about, /reviews, /videos, m.facebook.com and mbasic.facebook.com either redirected to login or returned the same single image). BBB, Birdeye, Houzz and Nextdoor have no real business photos (Houzz's only image is a generic stock boxwood-hedge placeholder, excluded as unverifiable). Bing/Google image search, the Wayback Machine (blueribbonlawns.com's old GoDaddy site used only generic stock photography, no real work photos) and Yelp (hard bot-block, 403 on every request) were also dead ends. BREAKTHROUGH: this environment has a global Playwright install with a Chromium binary at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome. Using the exact fixed-launch pattern documented in scripts/ig_scrape_fixed.js (full chrome binary, not headless_shell, with --disable-quic --disable-features=QUIC,EncryptedClientHello,PostQuantumKyber,UseDnsHttpsSvcbAlpn --ssl-version-max=tls1.2 to get through this sandbox's TLS-terminating proxy), a headless browser loaded https://www.facebook.com/BlueRibbonLawns/photos anonymously and Facebook's own client-side JS populated the DOM with the full public photos grid before showing its login interstitial. Scraped 66 tags, deduplicated to 65 unique photos by Facebook's internal photo ID, downloaded every one with curl (Chrome UA + Referer header), verified each with `file` (all valid JPEG/WebP, 13KB-384KB). Built a contact-sheet grid (8 cols) and visually reviewed all 65 before selecting.
images.curation_note: Excluded from consideration: every marketing/quote graphic with text overlay (hiring ads, holiday greetings, 'I came I mowed I kicked grass' meme, award-nomination graphics, a business-card-style flyer graphic, a hats/merchandise close-up). Kept only real photographs: finished lawns and landscaping at real client properties (the large majority of the 65), two crew-at-work action shots (a crew member holding a large tree limb lakeside; a crew member back-on digging out a stump/root ball, wearing a shirt with the company's round logo patch), and one branded-truck-and-trailer equipment shot cropped out of a 4-photo Facebook collage graphic (the collage itself has 'Blue Ribbon Lawns Inc.' text baked in and was not used whole; the truck-and-trailer quadrant was cropped out because it is a clean, text-free real photo of their actual rig). No selfies, no closed eyes, no piecemeal problem, no owner portraits used as gallery tiles.

brand_vibe: Real branding recovered from Facebook photos and the truck wrap: bold royal/sky blue cursive 'Blue Ribbon Lawns' logo on a black camo-wrapped truck, white phone-number decal, blue trailer. Built on light-v2 (clean white/cream base, easy-to-read black ink) with a blue accent (hue 208) derived via derive.py's hue-rotation system to match the real logo blue, letting the abundant real green lawn photography provide the organic contrast instead of defaulting to a generic landscaping green palette.
build_notes: Derived from templates/light-v2/index.html via content.json + scripts/derive.py, following the prestigeautocargo variant-adaptada pattern (FORGE-BRIEF 0.b): no fixed price list (services cards use 'ask about it' / free-estimate CTA instead of prices), no booking flow (CTA is tel: click-to-call, Facebook as secondary channel), a real Google map embed since the business address is consistently verified public data across BBB/Birdeye/Houzz. social_proof uses 'testimonios' mode with 3 real verbatim Google reviews (not 'razones' mode) since verifiable reviews with full author names exist. Two manual post-derive patches applied (documented precedent: output/bonzailandscapingportstlucie did the same): the CTA-final secondary button and the footer social link both literally said 'Instagram' in the frozen skeleton text (derive.py only swaps the URL/handle values, not that hardcoded label), patched to 'Facebook' since this business has no Instagram. Also fixed a double-period artifact in the footer copyright line ('Blue Ribbon Lawns Inc..' -> 'Blue Ribbon Lawns Inc.') that resulted from the brand name itself already ending in 'Inc.'. Gate passed clean: 0 em-dashes, all 10 image assets exist and decode, JSON-LD valid, all v2/v3 motion markers present, applyLang/<html lang> both 'en', no forbidden leftover strings from the light-v2 (Lash Bloom) skeleton. Visually verified end-to-end via a full-page Playwright screenshot after scripted incremental scrolling (to trigger the reveal-on-scroll IntersectionObserver system) before capture.
